correctness.rationale: An independent exact census normalized ternary quadratics, tested their polar determinants, recovered 234 distinct four-point conics and 4,641 unions of two distinct conics, and tested all 8,192 supports via the number of distinct intersections. Face counts at sizes 0–7 are 1,13,78,286,715,1287,1716,1638, with no larger faces; the entire exceptional seven-set list is the 78 distinct double-line supports. Every six-face extends to a seven-face; independently, two different double-line supports intersect in at most five points, so a six-set has at most one forbidden one-point extension. Enumeration of all 5,616 projectivities gives facet orbit sizes 234, 468 and 936. The obstruction to isolating the crossing of the two lines follows from uniqueness of the tangent to a smooth conic. The check is exhaustive only for rational point membership in PG(2,3), with two distinct nonsingular conics.
residual_risks: The finite check says nothing about larger fields, other concept classes or adaptive shattering.
